hints.title: Prefix Balance Transformation
hints.text: Replace zero with negative one. A subarray has more ones than zeros if its prefix sum difference is strictly positive.

hints.title: Inversion Counting Formulation
hints.text: We need to count pairs of indices j less than i such that prefix sum at j is strictly less than prefix sum at i.

hints.title: Offset Binary Indexed Tree
hints.text: Because prefix sums range from minus N to plus N, shift prefix sums by N plus one and query smaller prefix frequencies using a Fenwick tree.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def subarraysWithMoreZerosThanOnes(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        mod = 10**9 + 7
        n = len(nums)
        offset = n + 1
        tree = [0] * (2 * n + 5)
        
        def query(idx: int) -> int:
            s = 0
            while idx > 0:
                s += tree[idx]
                idx -= idx & (-idx)
            return s
            
        def update(idx: int, val: int) -> None:
            while idx < len(tree):
                tree[idx] += val
                idx += idx & (-idx)
                
        update(offset, 1)
        curr_pref = 0
        ans = 0
        for x in nums:
            curr_pref += (1 if x == 1 else -1)
            ans = (ans + query(curr_pref + offset - 1)) % mod
            update(curr_pref + offset, 1)
        return ans
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) using a Fenwick tree over shifted prefix range of size 2N
complexity.space: O(N) for Binary Indexed Tree storage
variables: N: number of elements in nums
complexity.notes: BIT operations take logarithmic time per array element.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Pairwise double loop yields quadratic running time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Binary indexed tree counts strictly smaller prefix sums in O(log N).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should convert 0/1 subarray balance into prefix inversion counting via Fenwick tree.
